From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: production: rising 5xx + long tail latency on reserved pool (samples attached)

Quick triage: initial metrics show sustained queue depth on CSP-1875's dedicated GPU pool starting ~07:35 UTC. Headroom has been eaten by sustained concurrent spike plus an increase in average sequence length for one of their models (model-1024-v2). We see elevated KV cache churn — cache misses are spiking and causing additional compute.

Immediate short-term mitigations (we can implement in the next 10–30 min):
- Enable emergency burst nodes (pre-approved ephemeral capacity) to relieve queueing for 60–90 minutes. Requires quick approval for billing/overage.
- Apply an emergency routing policy: divert new traffic to a compatible hosted model variant with slightly higher latency but lower tail errors (will involve rolling canary).
- Add a prefix cache bypass for the problematic model to reduce KV churn (risk: slightly higher compute per request).

Medium-term (2–8 hours):
- Roll a hotfix to model pinning and a config change to cap per-account concurrent inference tokens.
- Restart a subset of the affected workers (canary first).

I'll start the burst enablement if Priyom/exec sign off on the overage. Vivek, can you validate the model variant suggestion and confirm a safe canary window? Marissa, draft the customer note with the proposed 60–90 minute mitigation window.

— Rishi (SRE — serving runtime)

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Date: 2026-11-18T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: production: rising 5xx + long tail latency on reserved pool (samples attached)

I dug into the traces: model-1024-v2 has seen a change in token distribution from ClearStream's latest release (more long-sequence usage). That increases KV cache misses and OOM pressure on certain quantized workers. Two immediate actions I recommend:

1) Rolling restart of the 8 workers running the affected variant but in a staggered canary (2 -> 2 -> 4 across 30 minutes). This will reclaim memory and apply a config change to bump kv_cache_size by 15%.
2) Canary route ~20% traffic to hosted-model-compat-1024 (lower throughput but improved tail behavior) while we observe. If tail errors drop, expand to 50% and continue.

I can orchestrate the restart and routing; estimated user-visible relief in ~20–40 minutes after actions begin. We will monitor the token latency and 5xx rate and report every 15 minutes.

I'll prepare a short postmortem template after we stabilize.

— Vivek (Runtime Engineering)

Sara / ClearStream leadership —

Summary & plan: after triage we identified that recent release traffic patterns increased average sequence lengths causing KV cache churn and worker memory pressure on the dedicated pool. Immediate actions completed:
- Emergency burst nodes enabled for 90 minutes (traffic relieved; queue depth down 65%).
- Rolling canary to hosted-model-compat-1024 started; currently at 30% traffic and tail errors down from 12% to 2.8%.
- Staggered restarts of affected workers in progress; kv_cache_size bumped +15%.

Next steps & asks:
1) We propose a one-time operational credit of 10% for this billing period while we finalize the root cause and verify mitigations. Marissa will send formal language for approval.
2) Priyom / Jonas: please confirm approval for the burst overage (estimate provided in related link) so we can finalize billing and avoid invoice friction.
3) ClearStream: please confirm no bulk replays for the next 6 hours and share any other release changes that could impact sequence length.

Links & artifacts: SUP-4532 (ticket tracking), runbook (https://docs.redwood.example/runbooks/queue-choke-mitigation). Attachments: shared error sample and short logs.

We will send an internal postmortem and the customer-facing summary within 24 hours. If you'd like an exec-level sync, Jonas is available this afternoon.

— Vanessa Ortiz
